terms.text: A time without a break in which the Sun is above the horizon and below the Sun ceiling of a lunar region. We count spells of 2 hours or more.
One of the 36 parts of our year. Each part has 10 days, from 1 Jan. The last part has 15 days, to complete the year.
The highest angle of the Sun at a lunar region, in degrees above a level horizon. It is 2.08 degrees at Connecting Ridge and 7.90 degrees at Peak near Cabeus B.
The line where the land meets the sky, as seen from an area. Hills make the horizon higher and can hide a low Sun. Our horizon comes from Copernicus DEM GLO-90 elevation data.
How often the satellite snow maps of October 2015 to September 2025 show the ground free of snow in a given ten-day period.
In Antarctica, we count only the time from 27 November to 1 March, when the rock maps show bare ground. Snow is not measured there.
A pale rock that is mostly plagioclase feldspar. Much of the bright highland crust of the Moon is this type of rock. Our rock match looks for it.
A square of ground of approximately 11 km. It is the unit of our map and our lists. One figure gives the value for all of the area.
A candidate landing region near the Moon's south pole whose light we copy.
